newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares rallied for the fourth consecutive day on heavy foreign and local buying, which sent packaging stock Malbak surging and the financial index to a fresh high.

Dealers said that renewed talk of an interest rate cut in the third quarter of the year propped up banking shares, which together with other heavyweights also received a boost from futures-related arbitrage deals.

"There is generally positive sentiment on the market. The financials are especially strong as a cut in interest rates would relieve pressure on their margins and as they have had superior returns," a dealer said.
The financial index soared over 122 points or 1.3 percent, helping the industrial index gain 41.5 points to 8,469.9. The industrial index has put on over 220 points so far this week.

Gainers amongst banking stocks included Investec which rose 5.1 percent to 175 rand after recent good results and RMB Holdings which added six percent to 12.50 rand. It said earlier this week it would enter the retail market.
Malbak jumped over seven percent to 724 cents on rumours tobacco and industrial group Remgro was set to buy it, increasing its 18 percent holding.
But Remgro managing director Thys Visser declined to comment on the market speculation.
"We've not decided what to do regarding our investment or the future of Malbak," he told Reuters.
Other records were broken on the bourse with the all-share index jumping to a new high of 7,218.5, up 45.7 points and beating a previous 7,214 set on May 14.
The Johannesburg Stock Exchange also said that market capitalisation touched a record of 1,234 billion rand on Wednesday, above the 1,233 billion recorded on May 14.

Dealers said turnover on Thursday was high at over 920 million rand, boosted by several large bookovers in stocks including Clinics after it cautioned earlier that it was in talks. Black empowerment group Real Africa and food group Foodcorp also saw cross trades.
"The strength and interest was broadly based," a dealer said.

Smaller stocks were also busy including Usko which traded over 6.8 million shares and rose seven cents to a new year high of 60 cents after some respected funds took a stake in it. Consmining was active trading over 6.14 million shares.

Publico and parent Pubhold fell nine and 16.6 percent respectively on profit-taking after news Primedia had bought a stake in Pubhold. The shares had enjoyed a rally on Wednesday on rumours of a deal.
Platinum stocks were chased as the white metal fixed at $440, its highest level since September 1995. Amplats lifted 100 cents to 32 rand and Implats put on 125 cents to 51 rand.
Gold stocks were one of the few sectors shunned on the day as bullion slipped to near the $340 level. The index ended off 5.4 points at a fresh 50-month low of 1,140.3.
Equity index futures held firm on the day but were off their highs in late dealings.
The June all-share contract was at 6,520/28 from 6,508, the industrial contract was at 8,140/53 from 8,126 and the gold contract at 805/20 from 802.
